_about: Lore data (docs/lore/README.md; decisions 257, 258): entries with facts, each fact saying who knows it. Code uses only status agreed. Facts, never lines to say.

entries.name: the priest
entries.summary: The priest who keeps the town's temple and brings the fallen back.

facts.text: The town's priest brings the fallen back.
The priest blesses a thing brought to him for an offering of half its worth.
The priest's keep comes from the temple's alms, and the town pays him nothing while it is a hamlet.
The priest is at the temple from six till noon and again through the afternoon, and at the square at noon and in the evening.
Beneath the temple lies the town's crypt, where the wealthy are laid in their families' tombs, and the Mound-breakers have broken into it from outside.

entries.name: the medicine man
entries.summary: The medicine man who lives in the healer's hut in the wilds and brings the fallen back.

facts.text: The medicine man in the healer's hut brings the fallen back.
The medicine man gathers herbs near his hut and makes remedies, stamina potions, the bear's-claw charm and the bear's-grease draught, remedies first while anyone is sick.
The medicine man takes someone into his care for ten gold, or five herbs or five antlers, or for doing his first errand; only those in his care are brought back at his hut.
The medicine man visits the sick in town, and mends his hut with wood and cloth from the town's store.

entries.name: the smith
entries.summary: The town's smith, who went below the castle after a rumoured great dwarven forge with hired guards; ambushed and captured, he is held at the forge, forced to work goblin weapons for the Blood Rot's raids (docs/lore/castle.md).

facts.text: Rumour tells of a great dwarven forge deep below the castle.
The smith went down after the great dwarven forge, bringing an expedition of hired guards to protect him and carry out what they found.
The smith is held at the great dwarven forge, forced to work goblin weapons that supply the Blood Rot's raids.
The hired guards' remains and gear lie on the way down to the great dwarven forge.
The smith's name.

entries.name: the smith's hammer
entries.summary: The hammer taken with the smith.

facts.text: Whether the hammer has a name of its own.

entries.name: Wren
entries.summary: Wren is a woman, a companion who rests in town between trips; the rest of who she is comes from her card, which the companions tree rolls and grows.

facts.text: Wren is a woman who goes out with the town's people by choice and rests in town between trips.

entries.name: Pip
entries.summary: Pip is a young man, a companion who rests in town between trips and wants to become a squire; the rest of who he is comes from his card, which the companions tree rolls and grows.

facts.text: Pip goes out with the town's people by choice and rests in town between trips.
Pip is a young man.
Pip wants to become a squire.
Pip knows only enough to do the temple's work; part of his pay is to keep what he sees to himself, with the promise that he will one day become a holy knight of Theus.

entries.name: Nix
entries.summary: Nix is a woman, a companion who rests in town between trips; the rest of who she is comes from her card, which the companions tree rolls and grows.

facts.text: Nix is a woman who goes out with the town's people by choice and rests in town between trips.

entries.name: the taverner
entries.summary: The Mughouse's taverner keeps its counter and lives in the tavern (residents.json; economy's beds and rents).

facts.text: The taverner keeps the Mughouse's counter from nine in the morning till eight at night, and lives in the tavern.
Half of what the Mughouse is paid for its beds is the taverner's and the rest goes to the town's treasury: two gold for a resident's bed, two to six for a traveller's stay.
While the town has no cook, the taverner takes in the food, meat and fish brought to the Mughouse.

entries.name: the merchant
entries.summary: The town's merchant, the settled goblin with his counter a little apart, and the only fence (decisions 471, 586).

facts.text: The merchant sells dearer than the town's store does.
By day the merchant turns away anything stolen or taken from the dead.
By night the merchant buys stolen goods and grave goods across the counter, at half what the town would give.

entries.name: the cook
entries.summary: The cook in the town's kitchen (economy's kitchen; residents.json's cook day).

facts.text: The cook makes travel rations from food, roast meat from meat and roast perch from fish, for the shop's shelf and the town's daily meals.
The cook is at the well by five, in the kitchen from six till mid-afternoon, then at the square, and at the inn before going home.
When the well runs dry the cook works at half pace, and before the first harvest is in, nothing is cooked from the larder kept for the town's people.

entries.name: the carpenter
entries.summary: The town's carpenter, who raises and mends its buildings (economy's builds and repairs).

facts.text: The carpenter raises every building in town, repairs what is damaged and mends the roofs a storm breaks.
A build waits until its materials are in the store, and wood brought to the carpenter goes toward the build in hand.
The townsfolk pay the carpenter three gold every two days to keep their homes mended, and while the town has no fletcher the carpenter also mends arrows.

entries.name: the farmer
entries.summary: The town's farmer, once a field stands (economy's crop).

facts.text: The farmer sows in spring and harvests in autumn; rain helps the crop, a storm can flatten half of it, and a crop not in by winter rots.
In winter the farmer digs roots, and the farm's crop goes to the town's store, paid from the treasury.
The farmer is at the well by five and at work from six till four, then at the square, and at the inn before going home.
The hunter hunts deer, boar and rabbit in the wilds near the store, for the town has no hunting ground of its own.
The hunter sells meat and hides to the store, and the antlers and tusks are kept there.
Sometimes the hunter strays too far out, and whoever walks the hunter home is paid for it.

entries.name: the tanner
entries.summary: The town's tanner, once one comes and a tannery stands (economy's tannery).

facts.text: The tanner makes leather from hides, and bucklers and leather armour from the leather.
The tanner buys beasts' pelts for tanning, and claws, fangs, antlers and tusks for trimming leather.
The tanner's leather goes to the store, and the tanner's bucklers and armour to the shop.

entries.name: the woodcutter
entries.summary: The town's woodcutter at the woodlot (economy's woodcutter).

facts.text: The woodcutter fells trees at the woodlot's near edge, and a lot cut bare still gives deadwood.
The woodcutter sells wood to the store, and wood that others bring in goes to the carpenter.
The woodcutter is at the well at six, at the woodlot through the day, and at the inn at noon and in the evening.
